Preliminary analyses: Confirmatory 
factor analyses and measurement 
invariance
The eight items from the PTGI were specified to load 
onto one PTG factor, resulting in poor model fit: at T1 
χ2(20, N = 201) = 124.587, p < .05, CFI = .847, RMSEA = 
.161, and T2 χ2(29, N = 195) = 100.243, p < .05, CFI = 
.867, RMSEA = .143. Examination of factor loadings and 
modification indices revealed that items measuring the 
same theoretical domain of PTG were more similar. Thus, 
the residuals of the items measuring the same subscale of 
PTG were allowed to be correlated. In addition, Item 4 
shared variance with Item 1 and Item 10, and they were 
allowed to be correlated. This resulted in acceptable 
model fit at T1, χ2(14, N = 201) = 26.088, p < .05, CFI = 
.982, RMSEA = .066, and T2, χ2(14, N = 195) = 36.876, p < 
.05, CFI = .962, RMSEA = .092.

ABRA story with the teacher on a big screen and then completed a letter-sound or alphabetic activity as a whole group with teacher support.
Then, students typically worked on their own or in pairs for about 30–40 min on ‘word-level’ or ‘text-level’ skills while the teacher
circulated. Students were assigned to different levels of ABRA activities based on their current proﬁciency skills. Overall, observers rated
teacher instructions as clear and the activities as being chosen systematically and appropriately but did not observe any sign of connectivity
of ABRA learning to wider non-technology based learning themes.
